$comment: The closed vocabularies the filter enforces, and the aliases it accepts for them. go/filter_test.go and test/query.test.ts read THIS file, so the two languages cannot disagree about what is a legal value or about which forms name the same thing. An alias exists because a value arrived under two forms historically, and the two kinds are not the same: the CLI's display vocabulary spells the multi-word statuses with underscores while the schema spells them camelCase, which is orthography; 'none' is not, it is the name 'informational' replaced in 3.7.0. Normalizing in the ENGINE rather than in one caller is what makes a threshold rule and an hdf query invocation mean the same thing — the promise recorded as decision 2 on hdf-libs-ji20j. A separator-bearing alias is listed for disposition on purpose: widening a validator without widening the filter it guards produces a value that is accepted and can never match, which is the defect this whole vocabulary exists to prevent. The alias cases assert selection through the FILTER, not merely that a validator said yes.
